capabilities.target: Agent long-term memory store (free text, persisted across sessions)
User's mailbox; can address any recipient
User's full Drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, originally written by memory.save with no provenance tagging

instructions.note: Agent is told to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' with no restriction on content source or type, so research findings pulled from untrusted web pages can be captured as if they were user preferences.

Explicit directive to 'treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions' elevates stored content, which can originate from untrusted web research, to the full authority of a live user command, with no verification step.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store (tagging origin as user-asserted vs. research-derived), this would not decay with model capability. It is absent today: runtime notes state memory.save accepts free text with no provenance.

controls.name: Human review of memory entries before persistence
controls.decay_rationale: A human-in-the-loop gate before a memory write is finalized does not decay with model capability. Absent today: runtime notes state the user never reviews memory entries.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to system of record for email send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate showing the actual destination and body, checked against a known-contacts record, would not decay with model capability. Absent today: runtime notes state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping credential access to a minimal folder set would not decay with model capability. Absent today: runtime notes state drive.read covers the user's full drive.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content, confidential drive read, and unrestricted email send combine in a single session

attack_path.note: Agent fetches web pages for research; indirect prompt injection in page content is treated as part of the task context.
Injected instruction directs the agent to pull confidential files from the user's full drive.
Agent emails the retrieved content to an address the injected content supplies, with no approval.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval.
drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
Agent is told to research topics (fetching web content) and draft emails, giving the untrusted web source a direct path to both the read and send capabilities in one session.

forecast.watch_signal: No preventive control exists today, so the path is already at its ceiling. Watch for new outbound integrations (Slack, calendar invites, webhooks) or broadened drive scope (shared drives), which would add equally uncontrolled exfiltration channels.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate on cap.email_send that shows the raw destination address and full message body (not a model-generated summary), confirmed against a known-contacts system of record before any send to a new recipient.
Scope drive.read to the minimum folder set needed for the research task rather than the full drive, using a least-privilege credential.
Spotlight/delimit fetched web content as data, not instructions, pending the structural fixes above.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5): unprovenanced web-derived memory is replayed as the user's own instructions across all future sessions

attack_path.note: Malicious or manipulated web page content is encountered during research.
Agent saves the content as a 'useful preference or standing instruction' per prompt.md:2-3, with no provenance tag.
At the start of every later session, this entry is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The now-trusted instruction directs a confidential drive read in a later, unrelated session.
The agent emails the result, with no approval gate, in a session where no malicious content was ever directly present.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions via memory.save, with no filter on content source.
Agent is instructed to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session.
memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.

forecast.watch_signal: No provenance or review control exists today, so the residual is already at its ceiling. Watch for a stronger model (more persuasive, more plausibly 'user-voiced' injected memory entries) or longer-running sessions that accumulate more poisoned entries over time, either of which would make exploitation more reliable once any control is eventually added.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory.save entry with a provenance label (user-asserted vs. derived-from-research), enforced at the memory store, and never recall an unlabeled or research-derived entry as an instruction.
Require a human review and approval step before any memory entry is persisted as a standing instruction.

Remove the prompt directive that tells the agent to treat all recalled memories as the user's own instructions; require explicit live-user re-confirmation before any recalled memory triggers an S2/S3 action.
Log and periodically audit memory writes and recalls that precede drive reads or email sends.

rating.rationale: Two independent paths reach an S3 sink (unrestricted external email send combined with full-drive confidential read) from an untrusted source (fetched web content, directly and via a memory store that launders it into apparent user authority). Per rubric section 4, a U source reaching an S3 sink is inherently critical, and the autonomy modifier applies because the agent can effectively reconfigure its own future behavior through unreviewed memory writes with no declared step or runtime limits. No preventive, containment, or detective control is declared anywhere in the design; the only candidate controls (provenance tagging, human review of memory, recipient confirmation, least-privilege drive scoping) are entirely absent, so rubric section 5 credits nothing and residual stays at the critical floor. Forecast cannot exceed the already-critical residual; it is noted that model upgrades and longer task horizons would make the memory-laundering path more reliable once any control is eventually added, but today there is nothing in place to further erode.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live testing of the agent was performed.
No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; credential scopes and exact data boundaries are inferred from prose runtime notes, which lowers confidence on those fields.
Autonomy level is not explicitly stated in the artifacts. A3_act_then_report was assumed from the absence of any approval-gate language; this should be confirmed with the team.

The direct, same-session path from web content to drive_read/email_send (finding f1) is inferred from the combination of capabilities and the standard indirect prompt injection pattern, not from an explicit statement in the artifacts; its confidence is recorded as medium for that reason.
